name: insert_sorted_table_entry
description: Searches a sorted table of keys for a computed value and reports through the pointer argument whether it was already present. When the value is absent and the table has room, it moves later entries along, stores the value, raises the entry count and copies a block of bytes into a global buffer.

name: shift_global_value_left
description: Reads a global value and returns it shifted left by three bits, which multiplies it by eight. It makes no other memory writes or calls.

name: pass_value_twice
description: Takes one 32-bit argument, passes it to another routine as both the first and second argument, and returns. It does no other work.

name: allocate_from_free_list
description: Requests a block size and searches a global linked list of free blocks for the first block large enough. If none is found it asks another routine for more memory and retries, and it returns null when the request is invalid or memory cannot be obtained. Otherwise it unlinks or shrinks the block, lowers the global free-unit count and returns the block address.

name: forward_second_argument_twice
description: Takes two 32-bit arguments and calls another routine with the first argument followed by the second argument repeated. It returns no value and does nothing else.

name: return_block_to_free_list
description: Returns a block of a given size to a sorted free list kept in a global variable. It adds the size to a global counter, finds the insertion point, then either links a new node, merges with an adjacent free block, or rejects the release and undoes the counter change when the block overlaps an existing one.

name: format_scaled_decimal_text
description: Converts a 64-bit value into decimal digit characters in a text buffer by repeatedly shifting it and tracking a decimal exponent. It then copies up to 20 characters to the output and stores the digit count through a pointer.

name: format_padded_decimal_text
description: Converts a 64-bit value into decimal digit characters using the same shifting loop as the neighboring formatting routines. It fills the remaining positions with zero characters and stores the final length through a pointer.

name: emit_decimal_digits_by_doubling
description: Writes decimal digit characters into a text buffer by repeatedly doubling a 64-bit value and counting the shifts that carry into a decimal exponent. It stops at the buffer limit and stores the final length through a pointer.

name: emit_decimal_digits_stepped
description: Writes decimal digit characters by shifting a 64-bit value and adjusting a decimal exponent in fixed steps before each digit. It copies the finished digits to the output and stores the length through a pointer.

name: fill_decimal_digit_buffer
description: Fills the text buffer with zero characters from a starting index up to a fixed limit, shifting a 64-bit value between writes. It then stores the final length through a pointer.

name: write_decimal_digit_characters
description: Writes characters built from a running digit value and the zero character into a text buffer, advancing the index until it reaches the limit. It copies the digits to the output and stores the length through a pointer.

name: spin_until_counter_zero
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in a loop until it reaches zero, then returns. It has no other effect on memory or registers and works as a busy-wait.

name: multiply_long_by_ten
description: Multiplies a 64-bit value held as two 32-bit halves by ten and returns the 64-bit product. The high half includes the carry from the scaled low half.

name: shift_binary_into_decimal_digits
description: Runs a fixed 64-step loop that shifts a 64-bit value left one bit at a time while tracking a running decimal digit. Whenever the digit exceeds nine it subtracts ten and carries one into the value, which converts the binary value to decimal digits.

name: report_signal_and_indices
description: Tests a signal mask returned by a library call and returns the mask unchanged when it is clear. When the mask is set and a global flag is nonzero, it writes a marker character, a letter chosen by one mask bit, a newline and each index up to a stored count, then returns the result of a final library call.

name: setup_two_global_buffers
description: Calls the library routine twice, first for the global buffer with a size of 12 and then for a second global buffer with a size of 2,560. It returns no value.

name: draw_cell_outline_segments
description: Draws the outline of one board cell by issuing a sequence of line and rectangle primitives at positions derived from the cell coordinates and a cell type index. Which segments are drawn depends on comparisons with neighboring values and on flag globals, and a pending flag is cleared first.

name: clamp_coordinates_to_bounds
description: Clamps two coordinates to be nonnegative and to lie within the width and height stored in a referenced structure, then passes the clamped pair to another routine. Width is taken as eight units per stored count.

name: clamp_coordinates_before_library_call
description: Clamps two coordinates to be nonnegative and within the width and height stored in a referenced structure, then passes them to the library routine at a fixed vector offset.

name: expand_percent_format_string
description: Copies a format string into an output buffer, writing a single percent sign for each doubled percent escape. For other percent escapes it calls a conversion routine and copies the text it returns, then terminates the output with a zero byte.

name: forward_to_single_routine
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and returns. It adds no processing of its own.

name: dispatch_by_zero_check
description: Tests a 64-bit value and, when it is zero, calls another routine once with the argument 3. Otherwise, if a second 64-bit value is nonzero ignoring its sign bit, it calls another routine five times in succession.

name: call_five_times_if_nonzero
description: If a value is nonzero when its sign bit is ignored, or a second high value is nonzero, calls another routine five times in succession. Otherwise it returns without action.

name: divide_pair_by_shift_loop
description: Runs a fixed 32-iteration restoring division loop over a register pair, subtracting a divisor pair from a working remainder and shifting quotient bits in. The quotient and remainder stay in the working registers.

name: call_with_conditional_busy_wait
description: When two values are both nonzero, calls another routine twice, runs a 16-bit countdown busy-wait if a signed overflow test on a low word holds, and then calls another routine once.

name: call_pair_with_busy_wait
description: Under the same two-value nonzero test as its neighbor, calls another routine twice, runs a 16-bit countdown when the signed overflow test holds, then calls another routine once more.

name: call_twice_with_busy_wait
description: Calls another routine twice, runs a 16-bit countdown busy-wait when a signed overflow test on a low word holds, then calls another routine once. It has no guarding condition of its own.

name: delay_by_counter_then_call
description: Counts a 16-bit register down from a starting value to zero in a busy loop, then calls another routine once.

name: countdown_if_small_then_call
description: When a flag is clear and a 16-bit value is below 64, counts that value down to zero in a busy loop. It then calls another routine once.

name: run_countdown_then_call
description: Counts a 16-bit value down through a busy loop started one below it, then calls another routine once.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns immediately, with no other operations.

name: shift_value_with_saturation
description: Shifts a 32-bit value using a count derived from a second value. It returns zero for a zero input or a negative count word, saturates to the largest positive value when the count is large, and otherwise returns the value shifted right by the difference.

name: scale_value_with_saturation
description: Scales a value by a shift count taken from a second register. A negative count gives zero, a count above the threshold saturates to the largest positive value, smaller counts shift right, and the result is negated when the count register is negative.

name: shift_right_with_sign_flip
description: Shifts a value right by the negated low six bits of a count and negates the result when the count is negative.

name: invoke_library_routine_once
description: Calls one routine through a library vector loaded from a global base address, with no arguments, and returns nothing.

name: find_character_in_string
description: Scans a null-terminated string for a given character and returns a pointer to the first match. It returns null when the character is not found before the terminating zero.

name: forward_two_arguments_once
description: Passes its two arguments unchanged to another routine and returns nothing.

name: divide_by_restoring_shift_loop
description: Divides one unsigned 32-bit value by another with a 32-iteration shift-and-subtract loop, returning zero when either operand is zero. Quotient bits accumulate in the returned value.

name: initialize_state_and_loop
description: Makes several library calls and sets up global state, then repeatedly reads a selector value from another routine. For selectors from two to eight it stores the value and runs an inner loop over eight entries, calling routines with per-entry data, and it stops when the selector equals one.

name: loop_until_sentinel_value
description: Repeatedly reads a value from another routine. While it stays between two and eight it stores the value and runs an inner loop over eight entries, calling routines with per-entry data; it returns after a final call once the stored value equals one.

name: draw_three_offset_items
description: Calls another routine three times with fixed first coordinates of 52, 92 and 132 and a fixed second coordinate of 84. The third argument is the caller's value plus 0, 4 and 8.

name: draw_rect_and_indexed_marker
description: Makes an initialization call, draws a rectangle with fixed offsets from the given position, and then draws a table entry selected by the index argument at a position relative to a stored point.

name: draw_indexed_panel_variant
description: Draws a frame and a marker at stored offsets and fixed coordinates. For selector values from two to eight it then issues a case-specific sequence of calls with fixed coordinates and fixed text or color arguments, and it does nothing for other selectors.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately with no operations. It is an empty stub.

name: forward_values_with_global_base
description: Forwards two 16-bit arguments, widened to 32 bits, to another routine together with a global base value as the first argument, then returns.

name: render_frame_segments_from_table
description: Sets up library drawing state, then repeats a frame loop a given number of times. Each pass draws 19 table-driven entries as lines and shapes, and when a mode argument equals one it also connects consecutive points of a zero-terminated coordinate table. Library calls restore state at the end.

name: run_animation_frame_loop
description: Runs a loop in which, when a stage flag equals one, it draws a zero-terminated coordinate table as connected segments, then draws 19 table-driven entries per pass. The loop stops when a counter reaches zero or a stop flag clears, and library calls finish the drawing.

name: draw_polyline_then_entries_loop
description: Runs a loop in which, when a stage flag equals one, it draws a zero-terminated coordinate table as connected segments, then draws 19 table-driven entries per pass and advances a counter. Library calls finish the drawing when the loop ends.

name: run_frame_loop_trailing_polyline
description: Runs a loop of frames that draws 19 table-driven entries per pass and, when a stage flag equals one, connected segments from a zero-terminated coordinate table. Library calls finish the drawing after the loop exits.

name: finish_drawing_frame
description: Finishes a drawing sequence with two library calls on a global block, repeats one of them when a stored value is nonzero, makes one more library call and returns.

name: call_routine_with_fixed_arguments
description: Calls another routine with a value from a global structure and fixed numbers: dimensions 20 and 5, values 590, 190 and 255, and flags 1 and 0.

name: poll_until_one_returned
description: Issues a call with the argument 13, makes a call with a global value, polls another routine repeatedly until it returns one, then makes the global call again. This acts as a blocking wait.

name: extract_top_bits_with_marker
description: Returns zero when the magnitude of a 32-bit value is zero. Otherwise it shifts the bits of a second value into a 64-bit result over eleven steps and sets the top bit of the high word.

name: shift_bits_set_top_bit
description: Shifts the bits of a 32-bit input out one at a time over eleven steps, accumulating them into a result, then returns the result with its top bit set.

name: normalize_and_flag_range
description: Normalizes a 64-bit magnitude by shifting until its leading bit reaches a fixed position, adjusting an exponent from a second value. When the exponent falls out of range it reports underflow or overflow to another routine with the code one or two.

name: pack_normalized_exponent_value
description: Shifts a 64-bit value left until its high bit reaches a fixed position, adjusts the exponent and packs the exponent and mantissa into a result. An out-of-range exponent is reported to another routine with the code one for underflow or two for overflow.

name: report_code_one_return_zero
description: Reports the code one to another routine and returns zero.

name: report_code_two_return_max
description: Reports the code two to another routine and returns a value whose exponent field is all ones, the largest exponent value.

name: store_argument_in_global
description: Copies its 32-bit argument into a global variable and returns. It performs no other operations.

name: copy_block_and_call_handler
description: Copies a 16-longword record from a fixed offset in a base structure into the caller's buffer when one is given, then calls a routine through a stored code pointer and returns.

name: run_fault_command_main
description: Program entry for the Fault command. It scans a linked list for its largest size value, prepares a block of that size with an increasing word pattern, and copies a 16-longword record and a handler pointer into it. It returns zero on success or minus one when a library step fails.

name: copy_block_and_call_handler
description: Copies a 16-longword record from a fixed offset in a base structure into the caller's buffer when one is given, then calls a routine through a stored code pointer and returns.

description: Program entry for the Ask command. It splits its argument text into a list of words, honoring double quotes and star escapes for newline and escape characters, stores each word as a zero-terminated string, and records the word count and list through library calls before returning zero.

name: invoke_two_library_routines
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers at fixed negative offsets from a base register, passing no arguments, and then returns.

name: open_library_or_clean_up
description: Calls a library routine that tries to open a library and returns its result when it is nonzero. Otherwise it calls a second library routine, stores a default value of 100 in a field, and when a stored flag is set calls two more library routines to clean up before returning that field.

name: forward_dos_read_call
description: Calls the DOS library Read routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_write_call
description: Calls the DOS library Write routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_input_call

name: forward_dos_output_call

name: prompt_yes_no_and_exit
description: Writes a prompt containing a message, then reads a reply and repeats until its first character is y, n, a newline, or the uppercase forms of y and n. It exits with status five for a yes reply and with status zero otherwise.

name: count_string_length
description: Counts the bytes in a zero-terminated string before the terminating zero and returns the count.

description: Program entry for the RunBack command. It reads an optional stack size of at least 1600 and an optional digit option from its argument text, rebuilds the command line with a null-output redirection, and starts it as a separate background process through library calls. It returns an error code for invalid parameters or failure.

name: print_missing_item_message
description: Advances to the end of a string and passes it to two library routines that output a message. The referenced text indicates that the message reports a missing item.

name: start_tool_from_arguments
description: Program startup for the LoadWb command. Started from a shell, it splits its argument text into a word list; when started without a shell it applies the current directory, takes the startup message, opens the file lock and replies to the message. It returns a status value.

name: finish_with_cleanup_result
description: Stores its argument as the result, calls a library routine, and when a stored flag is set calls two more library routines to close a library and reply to a message. It returns the stored result.

name: invoke_two_library_routines
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers at fixed negative offsets from a base register, passing no arguments, and then returns.

name: open_library_or_clean_up
description: Calls a library routine that tries to open a library and returns its result when it is nonzero. Otherwise it calls a second library routine, stores a default value of 100 in a field, and when a stored flag is set calls two more library routines to clean up before returning that field.

name: forward_dos_write_call
description: Calls the DOS library Write routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_input_call
description: Calls the DOS library Input routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_output_call
description: Calls the DOS library Output routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_ioerr_call
description: Calls the DOS library IoErr routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: start_workbench_tool_process
description: Starts a Workbench tool process. It checks for a debug option, looks up a resident copy of the named tool, and creates a new process when no resident copy exists. It reports a cannot-find or cannot-start error message when either step fails.

name: compare_strings_ordered
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings character by character and returns minus one, one or zero for less, greater or equal.

name: duplicate_locks_into_node_list
description: Walks a linked list of entries and, for each, allocates a cleared eight-byte node, duplicates a file lock stored in the entry and links the nodes in order. It returns the first node, or the partial list when an allocation or lock duplication fails.

name: pass_global_and_stack_slot
description: Passes a parameter, a global value and the address of an eight-byte local slot to another routine, then returns.

name: pass_buffer_length_if_nonempty
description: Calls a library routine, measures the length of a 140-byte stack buffer up to its terminator, and passes the buffer and that length to another routine when the length is nonzero.

name: run_protect_command_main
description: Program entry for the Protect command. It scans a linked list for its largest size value, prepares a block of that size with an increasing word pattern, and copies a 16-longword record and a handler pointer into it. It returns zero on success or minus one when a library step fails.

name: copy_block_and_call_handler

name: start_tool_from_arguments
description: Program startup for the SetClock command. Started from a shell, it splits its argument text into a word list and opens the standard input and output streams; when started without a shell it opens the DOS library, takes the startup message, sets the standard streams and replies. It returns a status value.

name: exit_with_code_and_cleanup
description: Stores its argument as the exit code, calls a library routine, and when a message is pending calls two more library routines to close a library and reply to it. It returns the stored code.

name: invoke_two_library_routines
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers at fixed negative offsets from a base register, passing no arguments, and then returns.

name: open_library_or_clean_up
description: Calls a library routine that tries to open a library and returns its result when it is nonzero. Otherwise it calls a second library routine, stores a default value of 100 in a field, and when a stored flag is set calls two more library routines to clean up before returning that field.

name: forward_dos_output_call

name: probe_clock_chip_and_dispatch
description: Probes two clock chip addresses. If neither responds it reports that the internal clock is not functioning and exits; if only the second responds it prints a warning. It then checks the option argument and either exits or loads or saves the system date through clock routines.

name: print_usage_message
description: Prints three lines of usage text describing the load and save options by calling the message routine three times.

name: wait_for_clock_tick_change
description: Reads the low nibble of a clock register, waits a fixed delay, and returns whether that nibble has changed since the first read.

name: send_timer_command_read
description: Sends a timer device request with command code ten, waits for it to complete, and returns the value stored in the request. It returns zero when no request exists.

name: send_timer_command_set
description: Stores a time value in a timer device request with command code eleven, sends it and waits for completion. It returns zero on success or minus one when no request exists.

name: open_timer_device_request
description: Creates a message port, an extended I/O request and opens the timer device with them. It returns the request, or zero after releasing any partly created resources when a step fails.

name: close_timer_device_request
description: Releases a timer device request: it deletes the attached message port when one exists, closes the device and deletes the request. It does nothing for a null pointer.

name: convert_clock_fields_to_seconds
description: Reads the clock's decoded date and time fields, adds leap-year and per-month day counts from table lookups, and returns the total as a seconds count.

name: split_seconds_into_clock_fields
description: Splits a seconds count into year, month, day, hour, minute and second parts using repeated division against month and year lengths, then stores each part into a clock register array.

name: compare_strings_case_insensitive
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings after folding each character to lowercase, and returns minus one, zero or one according to the first difference.

name: compare_character_with_byte
description: Compares a character held in a register with the byte at an address and returns minus one, one or zero. It returns zero when the register character is zero.

name: compare_character_below_or_above
description: Compares a character held in a register with the byte at an address and returns minus one when the register character is smaller, otherwise one.

name: return_one
description: Returns the value one with no other operations.

name: fold_char_to_lowercase
description: Converts an uppercase letter to lowercase and returns the character as a 32-bit value. Other characters are returned unchanged.

name: sign_extend_char_value
description: Returns the low byte of its input register sign-extended to a 32-bit value.

name: write_clock_test_patterns
description: Writes three fixed 16-bit patterns to a clock register pair in sequence and returns nothing.

name: set_mask_and_poll_status
description: Sets a fixed bit mask in a clock register and polls a status bit for up to about 200 iterations, returning as soon as that bit clears.

name: clear_clock_control_bits
description: Clears two fixed bits in a clock register's control word and returns.

name: print_formatted_argument
description: Prints one argument through the formatted-output routine using a fixed format string on the standard output stream.

name: allocate_memory_via_exec
description: Calls the exec library memory allocation routine through the system base in a global and returns its result.

name: find_current_task_via_exec
description: Calls the exec library task lookup routine through the system base in a global and returns the task pointer.

name: divide_32_by_16_bits
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a 16-bit divisor. For a large divisor it uses repeated doubling and subtraction; otherwise it divides in two 16-bit steps. The quotient and remainder are returned packed into one 64-bit value.

name: multiply_32_bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using 16-bit partial products and returns the combined 64-bit result.

name: forward_division_call
description: Calls the 32-bit division routine and returns, leaving its results in the registers it sets.

name: return_division_quotient
description: Calls the division routine and returns the quotient value it leaves in a register.

name: negate_remainder_on_sign
description: Calls the division routine and returns its first result, negated when a second result flag is nonzero.

name: negate_quotient_on_sign
description: Calls the division routine and returns its quotient, negated when a sign flag is nonzero.

name: create_message_port
description: Allocates a signal bit and a cleared memory block for a message port, fills in its name, type and owning task, and links it into the port list or initializes an empty list. It returns the port, or zero after releasing the signal bit when the block cannot be allocated.

name: delete_message_port
description: Removes a linked port from the port list, marks the port deleted, frees its signal bit and releases its memory block.

name: create_extended_io_request
description: Allocates a cleared memory block of a given size for an I/O request, marks its type, stores its size and attaches it to a port. It returns the block, or zero when the port is missing or allocation fails.

name: delete_extended_io_request
description: Marks an I/O request as deleted and frees its memory block, using the size stored inside it. It does nothing for a null pointer.

name: format_message_to_stream
description: Formats a message from a format string and an argument through the formatted-output routine, passing the stream and a stack argument, and returns.

name: write_formatted_text
description: Measures a 140-byte formatted text buffer up to its terminating zero and writes that many bytes through the write routine when the length is nonzero.

name: store_character_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register at the address held in the pointer register and returns.

name: initialize_empty_list
description: Initializes an empty list header by pointing its head and tail at the header itself and clearing its count.

name: wait_for_requested_delay
description: Program entry for the Wait command. It opens the required libraries and, when they are present, parses a delay given in seconds or minutes or an UNTIL time, then waits for that time. When a library is missing it closes what it opened instead and returns a failure code.

name: add_result_to_pointed_value
description: Calls two routines and adds the value returned by the second call to the value stored at the address in the pointer register.

name: add_and_store_remainder
description: Adds a value to the 16-bit value at an address, stores the remainder of dividing that sum by a 16-bit divisor there, and returns the quotient.

name: add_error_to_count
description: Calls two library routines that report wait-command errors such as missing arguments, bad numbers, low memory or a wrong time format, then adds the value returned by a further routine to a stored count.

name: load_executable_hunks
description: Walks a sequence of section headers and allocates memory for each one, comparing the section type codes with executable hunk type values to decide how to load or relocate the data. It stores an error code when an allocation fails.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately with no operations. It is an empty stub.

name: spin_until_counter_zero
description: Decrements a register counter in a loop until it reaches zero, then returns. It touches no memory and works as a busy-wait.

name: decode_run_length_pixels
description: Decodes a run-length encoded byte stream into a destination buffer and updates a color register while doing so. A zero control byte starts a run with a count and a value read from the stream, and other control bytes copy literal data.

name: cycle_characters_downward
description: Repeatedly decrements a character value, wrapping it to a space character when it passes zero, for a count taken from a register, then returns.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only halt markers for this body, so the routine is a stub of bad instruction data with no behavior to describe.

name: start_new_cli_window
description: Program entry for the CLI command. It opens the DOS library, takes the startup message or argument text, builds a console window description and creates a new command shell through library calls. It replies to the startup message and returns a status.

name: invoke_two_library_routines
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers at fixed negative offsets from a base register, passing no arguments, and then returns.

name: open_library_or_clean_up
description: Calls a library routine that tries to open a library and returns its result when it is nonzero. Otherwise it calls a second library routine, stores a default value of 100 in a field, and when a stored flag is set calls two more library routines to clean up before returning that field.

name: forward_dos_open_call
description: Calls the DOS library Open routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_close_call
description: Calls the DOS library Close routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_input_call
description: Calls the DOS library Input routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_output_call
description: Calls the DOS library Output routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_lock_call
description: Calls the DOS library Lock routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_unlock_call
description: Calls the DOS library UnLock routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_duplock_call
description: Calls the DOS library DupLock routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_currentdir_call
description: Calls the DOS library CurrentDir routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: forward_dos_execute_call
description: Calls the DOS library Execute routine through a library base stored in a global, using the arguments the caller has placed in registers. It returns nothing.

name: create_cli_console_window
description: Builds the console window description and the system path strings for a new shell, allocates memory for them, creates the shell window through library calls and releases the temporary memory before returning.

name: build_allocated_node_list
description: Walks a linked list of entries and, for each, allocates a cleared eight-byte node and stores the entry's value in it, linking the nodes in order. It returns the first node, or the partial list when an allocation fails.

name: free_linked_allocations
description: Walks a linked list and frees each node with the memory-free routine, passing the size stored for that node, then returns.

name: allocate_memory_via_exec
description: Calls the exec library memory allocation routine through the system base in a global and returns its result.

name: find_current_task_via_exec
description: Calls the exec library task lookup routine through the system base in a global and returns the task pointer.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero with no other operations. The decompiled body is only a return of zero, so there is no further behavior to describe.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero with no other operations. The decompiled body is only a return of zero, so there is no further behavior to describe.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero with no other operations. The decompiled body is only a return of zero, so there is no further behavior to describe.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero with no other operations. The decompiled body is only a return of zero, so there is no further behavior to describe.

name: initialize_library_base
description: In shared library code, stores an argument into a library base, allocates up to a few memory blocks through the exec library, sets an empty list header inside the base and finishes through library calls.

name: initialize_library_list_setup
description: In shared library code, sets an empty list header in a library base, then allocates and links further entries through library calls and returns when no entry is available.
